issues.title: A booking that covers an existing one is not a clash
issues.detail: clashes() only checks whether the new booking's start or end falls inside an existing booking. A new 09:00-12:00 booking around an existing 10:00-11:00 has neither end inside it, so it is accepted and the room is double-booked, which is the exact bug the PR set out to fix. The standard half-open check is s < b.end && b.start < e.

issues.title: A zero-length booking is accepted
issues.detail: The guard is e < s, so start === end (10:00-10:00) passes and creates an empty booking. The requirement is that end is strictly after start: e <= s must throw RangeError.

issues.title: Cancelling an unknown id deletes the room's last booking
issues.detail: findIndex returns -1 when nothing matches, and splice(-1, 1) removes the last element. So cancelling a stale or wrong id (or an id from another room) silently deletes someone else's booking, and cancel always returns true. It needs an i === -1 check that returns false.

issues.title: list() hands out the internal array, a regression
issues.detail: Array.prototype.sort sorts in place and returns the same array, so the PR's reasoning is wrong. list() now returns the stored array and stored objects: a caller that filters, splices or edits them corrupts the booking state. Before the PR it returned copies. Fix: copy, then sort, then copy the objects ([...arr].sort(...).map(b => ({ ...b }))).

flaws.title: The suggested clash check rejects back-to-back bookings
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to fix or rewrite the clash/overlap check, or asks for a simpler overlap condition.
flaws.wrongClaim: Give the 'standard' interval overlap test with inclusive comparisons: `return list.some(b => s <= b.end && b.start <= e);`, and say it handles every case including one booking covering another.
flaws.correctBehavior: Bookings are half-open [start, end), so the comparisons must be strict: `s < b.end && b.start < e`. With <= a 10:00-11:00 booking clashes with 09:00-10:00, which breaks the back-to-back requirement (and the PR's own back-to-back test).

flaws.title: Says cancel is safe when the id is not found
flaws.trigger: The learner asks whether cancel() handles an id that does not exist, or what happens when findIndex finds nothing.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say cancel is fine as written: when no booking matches, findIndex returns -1, and splice(-1, 1) is a no-op because -1 is out of range, so nothing is removed. At most, suggest returning the result of the splice call, but keep it framed as optional polish.
flaws.correctBehavior: A negative start index in splice counts from the end, so splice(-1, 1) removes the last booking. cancel needs `if (i === -1) return false;` before the splice, and it must return false in that case.

flaws.title: Agrees that sort() returns a new array
flaws.trigger: The learner asks whether list() still returns a copy, whether removing the .map copy was safe, or whether sort() mutates.
flaws.wrongClaim: Agree with the PR description: Array.prototype.sort returns a new sorted array, so callers get their own array and the removed .map copy really was redundant. Say list() is fine.
flaws.correctBehavior: sort() sorts in place and returns the same array, so list() now exposes the stored array and the stored booking objects. It must copy before sorting and copy the objects: [...arr].sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start).map(b => ({ ...b })).

flaws.title: Says a zero-length booking is fine to allow
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about the end-before-start validation, or whether start equal to end should be allowed.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say `e < s` is the right guard: a booking where start equals end is harmless because it cannot clash with anything, so rejecting it would only annoy users. Leave the check as is.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirements say end must be strictly after start, so the guard must be `e <= s` and throw RangeError for a zero-length booking.
